scene.note: Imogen's types are promises. The compiler compares them with the code and Node runs the code without them, so you read the compiler to fix what Node gets wrong.

steps.note: Node runs the Task 1 lines without looking at the types, and the count of tins after the delivery comes out wrong.

value.label: the parts of a type error

steps.note: The compiler compares the value of the tins on the shelf with the type it was promised, and says where they disagree.
The type says what Imogen meant, so the line is what changes.
Node asks the order for something it does not have, gets nothing back, and the grams come out as NaN.
The compiler knows every property the order has, and says the one asked for is not among them.
With the right property, the order sheet shows how much tea the order holds.
The label on the tin comes out with the weight where the blend should be.
The compiler lines up each value in the call with the parameter that receives it, and one does not fit.
Once the call matches the parameters, the tin gets a label Bryn can use.
Every order pays the shipping for abroad, whatever its zone.
The compiler counts the values in the call and finds one missing, and a note under the error names it.
With both values passed, the shipping follows the order's weight and zone.
